title: Blocked rows satisfy achieved-completion checks
observed_behavior: blocked_with_reason belongs to TERMINAL_STATUSES, and require_complete rejects only statuses outside that set. A blocked row needs a note, reviewer, and non-inventory depth, but no completed semantic review, so it can satisfy the achieved-completion command.
expected_invariant: A strict exhaustive-completion result must distinguish completed review from blocked coverage and must fail while any required row remains blocked.
root_cause: The implementation uses one terminal-status set for both workflow finality and successful audit completion instead of defining a narrower achieved-status set for require_complete.
failure_scenario: A worker cannot inspect a file, marks it blocked_with_reason with nominal reviewer metadata, and the coordinator receives a successful --check --require-complete result despite an unreviewed repository path.
evidence: Static evidence: lines 30-39 include blocked_with_reason in TERMINAL_STATUSES.
Static evidence: lines 994-1010 treat every terminal status as complete and only require a reason for blocked rows.
Adversarial evidence: validation_findings for a first-party blocked row with reviewer, depth, and note returned an empty finding list.
Test evidence: the 12-test focused suite passed, while lines 93-117 cover pending and incompatible statuses but never assert that blocked rows fail achieved completion.
affected_flows: release and handoff evidence derived from terminal-row counts
existing_safeguards: Blocked rows must carry reviewer_notes; every terminal row must have a reviewer and semantic-looking review_depth; high-risk terminal rows require second_review_status complete.
safeguard_gap: Those shape checks do not prove review occurred and do not stop blocked rows from being counted as achieved completion.
tests_present: test_validation_rejects_missing_duplicate_and_false_terminal_claims verifies pending rows, incompatible line-review statuses, duplicates, missing paths, and high-risk second review.
tests_missing: A require_complete test asserting blocked_with_reason is reported as incomplete for every required category.
A CLI-level test proving the command exits nonzero and reports blocked-row counts.
recommended_remediation: Separate workflow-terminal statuses from successful-completion statuses; make require_complete reject blocked_with_reason, report blocked paths explicitly, and count only category-compatible verified/reviewed statuses as achieved.
remediation_risk: low: the change is confined to audit completion semantics but may expose previously hidden incomplete rows and require coordinator workflow updates.
validation_rung: Targeted Python unit tests plus an isolated CLI baseline containing complete, pending, and blocked rows; require nonzero exit until all blocked rows are resolved.
prior_audit_relationship: New audit-infrastructure defect; the ledger tool postdates the 2026-06-11 prior audit and directly affects the current exhaustive-completion goal.

title: Metadata files have no enforced compatible terminal status
observed_behavior: metadata/packaging is an allowed category but is omitted from LINE_REVIEW_CATEGORIES and the expected_terminal map. Any value in TERMINAL_STATUSES, including generated_verified or archive_inventoried, is therefore accepted for metadata during strict completion.
expected_invariant: Every file category must have an explicit, category-compatible completion status and validation must reject terminal statuses that make a different verification claim.
root_cause: The category enum was extended with metadata/packaging without extending the terminal-status model and compatibility table.
failure_scenario: A packaging manifest is assigned generated_verified without inspection of its packaging semantics; validation accepts it, so coverage reports complete even though no defined metadata review obligation was met.
evidence: Static evidence: ALLOWED_CATEGORIES includes metadata/packaging at line 53.
Static evidence: expected_terminal at lines 1000-1006 covers generated, vendor/runtime, binary, and archive categories only.
Adversarial evidence: validation_findings accepted a metadata/packaging row with generated_verified and returned no findings.
Test evidence: the only terminal-compatibility test uses a first-party source row; no metadata row appears in the 219-line test file.
existing_safeguards: Unknown categories and unknown statuses are rejected, and most non-line-review categories have a single expected terminal status.
safeguard_gap: An allowed category without a compatibility rule bypasses the safeguard entirely.
tests_present: test_validation_rejects_missing_duplicate_and_false_terminal_claims verifies one incompatible status for first-party executable source.
tests_missing: Table-driven compatibility tests covering every ALLOWED_CATEGORIES member.
A metadata/packaging success case and rejection cases for every unrelated terminal status.
recommended_remediation: Define a metadata-specific verified status or deliberately map metadata to line review, add it to the category compatibility table, and assert that the table exhaustively covers every allowed category.
remediation_risk: low: schema and worker-fragment migration is bounded, but existing metadata rows may need explicit status conversion.
validation_rung: Targeted table-driven unit tests for the full category/status cross-product plus a strict CLI check over representative metadata files.
prior_audit_relationship: New audit-infrastructure defect; the prior audit did not contain this status model.

title: Strict completion does not enforce semantic or reconciliation evidence
observed_behavior: Rows contain classification flags and PROJECT_INDEX reconciliation fields, but those fields are not required or validated at completion. Required semantic fields are checked only for presence; terminal first-party rows can retain empty reviewed sections, placeholder responsibility, default evidence, and prior_audit_coverage not_reconciled while passing require_complete.
expected_invariant: A terminal row must prove the review mode required by every applicable category/flag, identify reviewed scope and evidence, reconcile prior audit and generated index state, and reject inventory defaults masquerading as semantic review.
root_cause: The row schema conflates structural serialization with completion evidence: build_rows emits useful flags and defaults, while validation checks only a small subset of nonempty/compatible semantics and no multi-flag obligations.
failure_scenario: A coordinator bulk-updates review_status and reviewer fields without replacing inventory defaults; every path appears terminal although symbols, generated provenance, binary/archive/runtime obligations, PROJECT_INDEX drift, and prior findings were never reconciled.
evidence: Static evidence: REQUIRED_ROW_FIELDS lines 56-90 omit generated, vendor, archive, binary, runtime, evidence_snapshot, project_index_present, project_index_hash_matches, file_size_bytes, and git_mode.
Static evidence: build_rows lines 616-639 initializes inventory_only, empty reviewed sections, not_reconciled prior coverage, default commands, and index flags.
Static evidence: validation_findings lines 978-1018 checks field presence, status compatibility, reviewer/depth, finding IDs, and high-risk review but not the omitted/default semantic evidence.
Adversarial evidence: a line_reviewed_no_findings first-party row with empty reviewed sections/evidence and not_reconciled prior coverage returned no findings.
Test evidence: lines 63-117 provide nominal semantic fields but do not mutate them to empty/default values; lines 119-131 only assert that baseline Markdown avoids claiming review.
existing_safeguards: Terminal rows require a reviewer and non-inventory review_depth; with-findings rows require IDs; classification flags and index-presence/hash fields are emitted into baseline rows.
safeguard_gap: The emitted evidence is optional to validation, values may remain placeholders, and one primary category can hide other applicable obligations such as runtime plus binary.
tests_present: test_validation_rejects_missing_duplicate_and_false_terminal_claims exercises structural required fields and selected terminal failures.
tests_missing: Reject terminal rows with empty reviewed_symbols_or_sections, default evidence, placeholder responsibility, or not_reconciled prior coverage.
Require and validate classification flags and PROJECT_INDEX reconciliation fields.
Table-driven dual-obligation cases such as generated binary, archived binary, and bundled runtime binary.
A full CLI completion test that proves inventory-only defaults cannot become complete by changing status alone.
recommended_remediation: Define a versioned completion schema separate from inventory serialization; require all evidence fields, reject known defaults, enforce obligations derived from every true classification flag, and require explicit PROJECT_INDEX and prior-audit dispositions before terminal success.
remediation_risk: medium: tightening the gate will invalidate many existing worker fragments and requires a deliberate migration rather than silent coercion.
validation_rung: Unit tests for each semantic predicate and flag combination, fragment-schema migration tests, then end-to-end --write/--merge-reviews/--check --require-complete in an isolated repository.
prior_audit_relationship: New audit-infrastructure defect, but it risks repeating the 2026-06-11 audit's partial-coverage problem by allowing inventory metadata to stand in for semantic review.

title: Registry-critical paths can fall below the independent-review threshold

locations.symbol: build_rows risk selection and high-risk second-review state
registry risk and malformed-registry fail-closed tests

observed_behavior: At discovery, fallback risk used filename substrings and could classify a registry-critical storage path below the independent-review threshold. Current audit-ledger code now loads and validates RISKY_FILE_REGISTRY.v1.json, matches its globs case-insensitively, maps critical to high, combines registry and additive fallback risk conservatively, and fails closed for malformed registries.
expected_invariant: Risk and second-review obligations must conservatively include every current high/critical registry glob even when generated navigation data is absent, stale, or incomplete.
root_cause: Risk derivation is duplicated as an incomplete substring heuristic instead of loading and matching the maintained risky-file registry and boundary rules.
failure_scenario: PROJECT_INDEX omits or understates a source-movement script; the fallback marks it medium, the worker completes a single review, and strict completion accepts source/scratch/output mutation code without the required independent review.
evidence: Current source lines 728-786 validate and match the authoritative risky-file registry before applying additive fallback markers.
Current build_rows lines 979-1047 selects the stronger indexed/fallback tier and marks every high-risk row second-review pending.
Focused tests lines 222-245 require storage/move.ps1 to be high and malformed registry input to raise.
The fresh 6,499-row global gate classified the registry paths as high and exposed the full independent-review remainder.
existing_safeguards: Indexed and fallback tiers are combined using the higher value; several high-risk substrings are recognized; terminal high-risk rows require second_review_status complete.
safeguard_gap: The fallback is not registry-complete, and critical is not represented as a distinct tier, so authoritative path-glob obligations can disappear when index evidence is unavailable.
tests_missing: Table-driven matching for every high/critical RISKY_FILE_REGISTRY path_glob.
Index-missing and index-stale cases for storage, paths, cleanup, repair/reconcile, lifecycle, settings, rename, and network boundaries.
A completion test proving each registry-critical row requires independent review.
recommended_remediation: Implemented in the audit tooling: authoritative registry loading and deterministic glob matching are fail-closed, critical/high map to the strict high tier, and table-driven representative plus malformed-registry tests cover the fallback path.
remediation_risk: medium: changing risk assignment expands second-review workload and registry parsing must be deterministic across Windows path forms.
validation_rung: Registry parser/matcher unit tests for every entry, malformed-registry negative tests, and an isolated coverage build demonstrating required second review for representative critical paths.
prior_audit_relationship: New audit-tool defect; it conflicts with the repository's pre-existing risky-file registry and no-touch boundary contract.

title: Malformed or stale error evidence cannot block completion reliably

locations.symbol: main error merge and check actions

observed_behavior: Error validation checks required-key presence, ID uniqueness, linked_finding_ids array shape, and coverage_blocked boolean only. Empty strings, unknown classifications/dispositions, and nonnumeric exit codes pass. Strict coverage checking neither proves worker fragments were merged/current nor rejects unresolved coverage_blocked records or broken finding links.
expected_invariant: Every command failure, warning, and skip must be well-typed, use finite classifications/dispositions, link to existing findings, remain provenance-current, and block achieved completion while its coverage impact is unresolved.
root_cause: The error ledger is implemented as a separately merged reporting artifact without a validated domain schema or a dependency from --require-complete to current merged error state.
failure_scenario: A worker records a blocking review failure with malformed fields or leaves it only in a fragment; the coverage matrix reaches terminal statuses and --require-complete exits successfully without surfacing the unresolved evidence gap.
evidence: Static evidence: REQUIRED_ERROR_FIELDS defines names but no value domains.
Static evidence: error_record_findings lines 832-849 performs only four structural checks.
Static evidence: check_outputs lines 1068-1090 validates the coverage matrix and current file identity but never loads error fragments or ERRORS.jsonl.
Static evidence: --merge-errors and --check are independent CLI branches at lines 1117-1130.
Adversarial evidence: an error record with empty required strings, invented classification, and nonnumeric exit_code returned no findings.
Test evidence: lines 138-157 cover duplicate IDs and linked_finding_ids array shape only.
existing_safeguards: Missing keys, blank IDs, duplicate IDs, non-array links, and non-boolean coverage_blocked values are rejected during explicit error merge.
safeguard_gap: Semantic values, linkage, fragment freshness, merge provenance, and unresolved blocking disposition are not validated or consumed by completion.
tests_present: test_error_records_require_unique_ids_and_complete_shape verifies one nominal record, duplicate ID detection, and linked_finding_ids array shape.
tests_missing: Type and nonempty validation for timestamps, commands, directories, exit codes, summaries, phases, retry results, and dispositions.
Finite classification/reproduction/disposition enums and cross-field rules.
Finding-link existence and unresolved coverage_blocked completion tests.
Fragment-versus-central freshness and provenance tests.
An end-to-end check proving an unmerged or unresolved blocking error forces nonzero completion.
recommended_remediation: Introduce a versioned error-record schema with finite enums and cross-field validation; merge by explicit provenance; validate links against the current finding set; and make require_complete reject unmerged, stale, malformed, or unresolved coverage-blocking errors.
remediation_risk: medium: existing heterogeneous error records may require migration and the blocking lifecycle needs explicit resolved/deferred semantics.
validation_rung: Schema unit tests and malformed-record property cases, followed by isolated merge/check CLI tests for current, stale, linked, unlinked, resolved, and unresolved blocking errors.
prior_audit_relationship: New audit-ledger defect; current AUDIT-ERR-COVERAGE-009 already demonstrates why checker success must not be treated as sufficient completion proof.

title: Review merge can report success against stale worktree content
observed_behavior: A review fragment is compared with the hash stored in the existing coverage matrix, but merge_review_ledgers does not compare that baseline with current files before writing and printing success. Current hash/tracked/blob checks exist only in the later, separate --check path.
expected_invariant: A merge that claims review evidence was accepted must atomically verify the fragment, baseline, and current tracked content identity before mutating the matrix or reporting terminal counts.
root_cause: Baseline-relative fragment validation and worktree-relative content validation are split across independent CLI actions with no freshness precondition in the mutating merge path.
failure_scenario: A file changes after baseline creation; a fragment matching the stale baseline merges successfully and is reported terminal, creating a window where downstream consumers treat obsolete review evidence as current before a separate check runs.
evidence: Static evidence: review_fragment_findings lines 791-801 compares ownership and hash only to baseline_rows.
Static evidence: merge_review_ledgers lines 810-829 validates and writes without invoking current_content_findings.
Static evidence: current content SHA, tracked state, and Git blob checks exist at lines 1025-1052 but are reached only through check_outputs.

Current-worktree evidence: COVERAGE_MATRIX.jsonl still records engine hash 0b1d44fa... and test hash 8a75e1da..., while frozen files hash to a77c3d49... and 837cbb86... respectively; the companion current-hash fragment cannot be safely merged until baseline refresh.
Test evidence: lines 159-184 catches a fragment differing from a supplied in-memory baseline but never changes the underlying file after baseline creation.
existing_safeguards: Fragment worker and baseline hash mismatches fail; a later --check recomputes SHA-256, tracked state, and Git blob identity; content changes reset preserved review fields during a subsequent --write.
safeguard_gap: The safeguard is not part of the merge transaction, so merge can mutate and announce success before the required freshness check.
tests_present: test_review_fragments_enforce_hash_and_worker_ownership verifies worker ownership and fragment-to-baseline hash mismatch.
tests_missing: An isolated Git-repository test that changes content after baseline generation and expects --merge-reviews to fail without writing.
Tracked-state and Git-blob drift cases during merge.
A success test proving freshness validation occurs immediately before the atomic replacement.
recommended_remediation: Have merge_review_ledgers derive the current expected universe and call current_content_findings before applying fragments; write outputs atomically only after all validation succeeds and include verified baseline identity in the success report.
remediation_risk: low to medium: the behavior becomes fail-closed and may reject concurrent workflows that currently appear to merge, so callers need a refresh-and-retry path.
validation_rung: Isolated temporary Git repository tests for stale hash, staged content, rename/deletion, and clean merge, plus a CLI assertion that failed merges leave matrix bytes unchanged.
prior_audit_relationship: New audit-infrastructure defect; concurrent drift captured in AUDIT-ERR-COVERAGE-008 is a concrete trigger for this merge window.

title: Finding merge claims root-cause deduplication without performing it
observed_behavior: Finding validation rejects duplicate IDs but never compares root cause, locations, scenario, or evidence. merge_finding_ledgers sorts and writes every unique-ID record while both rendered Markdown and CLI output call the result deduplicated; semantic text, location range/currentness, relation targets, and central freshness are also unchecked.
expected_invariant: A central register advertised as deduplicated must apply a documented deterministic root-cause identity policy, retain provenance for merged reports, and validate that every finding's evidence and relationships refer to current, valid repository locations and IDs.
root_cause: The data model declares rich root-cause fields, but merge implementation performs only per-record shape checks and ID uniqueness; the deduplication claim was added without a grouping/merge algorithm or freshness contract.
failure_scenario: Two workers report the same defect under different IDs; both survive as separate P1/P2 items, counts and prioritization inflate, fixes split across duplicates, and later links may target inconsistent canonical records while the CLI reports successful deduplication.
evidence: Static evidence: finding_record_findings lines 704-731 tracks seen_ids only and validates a few array/value shapes.
Static evidence: merge_finding_ledgers lines 761-770 only sorts by severity and ID before writing.
Static evidence: findings_markdown line 740 and CLI line 1128 explicitly claim root-cause deduplication.
Adversarial evidence: two records with different IDs but identical root_cause, title, location, scenario, and evidence produced finding_record_findings([]) with no errors.
Test evidence: lines 186-215 cover valid shape, invalid severity, and empty locations only; they do not submit duplicate root causes.
affected_flows: finding counts, prioritization, and remediation ownership
existing_safeguards: Required keys, nonblank ID, unique ID, finite severity/disposition, nonempty location array, minimal location shape, and selected array fields are checked.
safeguard_gap: Unique IDs are not equivalent to unique root causes, and there is no canonicalization, merge provenance, semantic nonempty validation, location currentness/range validation, relation integrity, or fragment-to-central freshness check.
tests_present: test_finding_records_require_evidence_shape verifies one complete record and rejects invalid severity and an empty location array.
tests_missing: Two-ID identical-root-cause deduplication and conflict-resolution tests.
Near-duplicate normalization across path separators, overlapping locations, and equivalent scenarios.
Nonempty semantic text, valid line ranges, current paths/hashes, related-ID existence, and cycle handling.
Fragment-to-central freshness and deterministic provenance retention tests.
recommended_remediation: Define a stable root-cause fingerprint from normalized category, invariant/root cause, and primary location; group fragments by that identity; select or generate a canonical ID; merge locations/evidence/provenance deterministically; validate semantic/link/location integrity; and report unresolved dedup conflicts instead of claiming success.
remediation_risk: medium: incorrect automatic coalescing could hide distinct defects, so start with deterministic exact/strong matches and require explicit review for ambiguous clusters.
validation_rung: Unit and property tests for exact duplicates, near duplicates, distinct same-location defects, deterministic ordering, relationship rewriting, and invalid locations, followed by an end-to-end fragment merge snapshot test.
prior_audit_relationship: New audit-infrastructure defect; the current audit goal explicitly requires findings to be deduplicated by root cause, which the prior audit tooling did not enforce centrally.
